name: AquaFlow: Water Delivery Operations
tag: Order intake, route planning, jug inventory and reports for water delivery businesses, in one place.

scenarios.title: Plan tomorrow's deliveries
scenarios.ask: We have {orders} orders for tomorrow and {trucks} trucks. Plan the routes.
steps: Collected {orders} orders from the website, phone notes and repeat schedules.
Split them into {trucks} routes of about {=round(orders / trucks)} stops each, grouped by neighborhood.
Each truck needs about {=round(orders * jugs / trucks)} full jugs and room for empties.
Queued text messages with a 2-hour delivery window for every customer.
followups: What if a truck can't carry that many jugs?
Set each truck's capacity and the router splits overloaded routes or adds a reload stop at the warehouse.
Can drivers see the route on their phones?
Yes. Each driver gets a stop list with directions, gate codes and notes, and marks deliveries done as they go.

scenarios.title: Keep jugs in stock
scenarios.ask: We have {stock} full jugs and go through about {daily} a day. Our supplier takes {lead} to deliver.
steps: Counted {stock} full jugs and {=round(stock * 0.4)} empties waiting for refill.
Usage runs about {daily} a day, higher on Mondays.
Stock covers about {=round(stock / max(1, daily), 1)} days. Reorder point is {=daily * (lead + 2)} jugs, which includes a 2-day buffer.
Drafted a purchase order for the supplier, waiting for your approval.

result.title: Stock plan
rows: {=max(0, daily * (lead + 2) - stock)} jugs short of the reorder point

followups: Does it track empty jugs customers still have?
Yes. Each customer has a jug balance, and drivers record empties picked up so deposits stay accurate.
It can, but by default it drafts the order and waits for you.

scenarios.title: Monthly business report
scenarios.ask: Give me last month's numbers: {customers} customers, about {churn}% cancelled.
steps: Pulled orders, payments and cancellations for the month.
Lost {=round(customers * churn / 100)} customers. Most said delivery windows were too wide.
Suggested narrower delivery windows in the two areas with the most cancellations.
followups: Where do cancel reasons come from?
From a one-question survey sent when a customer cancels, plus driver notes. You can edit the reasons list.
Can I send this to my accountant?
Yes. The report exports as a PDF or a spreadsheet.
